elements.name: Stream Buffer
elements.what: RTOS kernel object providing a single-writer single-reader byte stream (message-buffer variant: discrete variable-length messages) with blocking send/receive and a trigger level controlling how many bytes must arrive before the reader unblocks.
elements.problem: Passing continuous byte data or framed messages from exactly one task/ISR to exactly one task; the single-reader/single-writer restriction permits a much lighter implementation than a general message queue while keeping blocking semantics.
elements.named_in: freertos.org 'RTOS Stream Buffers' (title verified live 2026-07-10); Mastering the FreeRTOS Real-Time Kernel ch. Stream and Message Buffers
elements.borderline: blocking kernel-object layer over an SPSC ring buffer (cf. existing spsc-lock-free-ring-buffer); kept because trigger-level blocking byte/message-stream semantics is a distinct named kernel mechanism, not just the underlying data structure

elements.name: Direct-to-Task Notification
elements.what: Each task carries built-in notification slots (a 32-bit value plus pending state) that other tasks or ISRs can set, increment, overwrite, or OR bits into, letting the task block on its own notification instead of on a separate kernel object.
elements.problem: Binary/counting semaphores, event flags, and one-deep mailboxes used purely to wake a single known task cost a separate kernel object and slower code paths; notifying the receiving task directly is significantly faster and uses less RAM when there is exactly one receiver.
elements.named_in: freertos.org 'Direct to task notifications' (title verified live 2026-07-10); Mastering the FreeRTOS Real-Time Kernel; CMSIS-RTOS2 Thread Flags API

elements.name: Event Flags Group
elements.what: A kernel object holding a word of boolean event bits that tasks and ISRs set or clear atomically and that tasks block on with AND/OR combinations of bits, optionally auto-clearing the bits on wake.
elements.problem: A task must wait for any-of or all-of several distinct conditions signaled by different tasks/ISRs; semaphores signal only a single anonymous event and compose poorly for conjunction/disjunction waits.
elements.named_in: freertos.org 'FreeRTOS event groups' (title verified live 2026-07-10); CMSIS-RTOS2 osEventFlags API; ThreadX event flags group; uC/OS-III event flags

elements.name: Software Timer
elements.what: Kernel facility multiplexing many logical one-shot or auto-reload callback timers onto a single hardware tick/timer, with expiry callbacks typically executed by a timer-service (daemon) task rather than in interrupt context.
elements.problem: Applications need many independent timed callbacks but hardware timers are scarce; a software timer layer provides unlimited cheap timers without dedicating a hardware timer or a task per delay.
elements.named_in: freertos.org 'FreeRTOS software timers' (title verified live 2026-07-10); CMSIS-RTOS2 osTimer API; Zephyr k_timer docs
elements.borderline: decision logged: index has timer-wheel, but that is an implementation data structure for large timer populations; the RTOS software-timer kernel facility (one-shot/auto-reload objects + timer daemon) is the mechanism designers name and reach for, so a separate element is warranted

elements.name: Idle Task Hook
elements.what: A user callback invoked repeatedly from the RTOS idle task (the lowest-priority always-ready task), used to run work that should consume only otherwise-idle cycles: low-power sleep entry, background self-tests, stack watermark checks.
elements.problem: Firmware has background work and power-management actions that must run only when nothing else is runnable, without a dedicated task or any interference with real-time work.
elements.named_in: freertos.org 'The Idle Task and the Idle Task Hook'; Mastering the FreeRTOS Real-Time Kernel; uC/OS-II OSTaskIdleHook
elements.borderline: arguably just a registered callback (hook method) into the scheduler; kept because idle-context background processing is a named, recurring firmware mechanism across RTOSes (FreeRTOS idle hook, Zephyr idle thread, uC/OS idle hook) with distinct constraints (must not block)

elements.name: Flash Translation Layer
elements.what: A firmware layer that remaps logical block writes to out-of-place physical flash pages, maintaining a logical-to-physical mapping table plus garbage collection so erase-constrained flash presents an ordinary rewritable block device.
elements.problem: NAND/NOR flash cannot rewrite in place and erases in large blocks with limited endurance; out-of-place remapping hides erase-before-write, enables wear leveling, and keeps a consistent mapping across power loss.
elements.named_in: Intel 'Understanding the Flash Translation Layer (FTL) Specification' (AP-684, 1998); Chung et al., 'A survey of Flash Translation Layer', Journal of Systems Architecture 2009
elements.borderline: composite mechanism (composes flash-wear-leveling + out-of-place update + garbage collection); kept because FTL is the established name for the mapping mechanism itself, which the existing flash-wear-leveling entry does not cover

excluded_notable.name: Zephyr memory slab (k_mem_slab)
excluded_notable.why: Dedup: despite the name it is a fixed-size block pool, i.e. already covered by pool-allocation (aka fixed-block allocator, partition allocator). It is NOT the Bonwick object-caching slab-allocator; folding it there would be wrong. Recommend adding 'memory slab (Zephyr)' as an aka of pool-allocation.

excluded_notable.name: Workqueue (Zephyr k_work / Linux workqueue)
excluded_notable.why: Dedup: same mechanism as deferred-interrupt-processing, whose aka list already contains 'work queue deferral' (plus tasklet, softirq, DPC). No new element.

excluded_notable.name: Stack overflow detection hook (vApplicationStackOverflowHook / FreeRTOS methods 1 & 2)
excluded_notable.why: Dedup: the detection techniques are already covered by stack-painting-watermarking (fill-pattern check, method 2) and guard-page/MPU redzone; FreeRTOS method 1 (SP bounds check at context switch) is an implementation detail, and the hook itself is a plain callback, not a distinct mechanism.

excluded_notable.name: Interrupt latency budgeting
excluded_notable.why: Practice/analysis activity (budget allocation and measurement), not an implementable in-program mechanism; fails the altitude test downward into process territory.

excluded_notable.name: Tick hook (vApplicationTickHook)
excluded_notable.why: Plain periodic callback from the tick ISR; unlike the idle hook it carries no distinct execution-context semantics beyond 'callback registered in ISR context' — covered by callback + interrupt-service-routine.

excluded_notable.name: Flash journaling / journaling filesystem
excluded_notable.why: Dedup: write-ahead-log already carries 'journaling' in its aka; a journaling FS is WAL applied to filesystem metadata. Power-loss-resilient update in flash is otherwise covered by copy-on-write + shadow-paging + eeprom-emulation-in-flash.

excluded_notable.name: littlefs metadata pairs / CTZ skip-list
excluded_notable.why: Named only in the littlefs DESIGN.md; single-project construct names that fail the 'recurring across codebases' gate. The recurring mechanisms littlefs composes (copy-on-write, wear leveling, checksummed commit) are already in the index.

notes: Gap-hunter rtos-embedded2. Verification: four FreeRTOS mechanism names (stream buffers, direct-to-task notifications, event groups, software timers) verified at title level on live freertos.org pages this session; FTL named in Intel AP-684 spec and the Chung et al. 2009 survey (canonical literature, not fetched). Decision log: (1) software-timer added as a kernel-facility element distinct from the existing timer-wheel implementation structure — rationale recorded in the element's borderline field. (2) Stream Buffer and Message Buffer folded into ONE element (message buffer = framed variant built on stream buffer). (3) Event Flags Group added beyond the charter's explicit list: a classic cross-RTOS primitive (FreeRTOS/ThreadX/uC-OS/CMSIS) absent from the index under any alias — checked against eventcount, reminder, latch, semaphore entries. (4) Zephyr memory slab and workqueue deliberately NOT added (dedup calls above). Flagged possible gap outside my charter: MPU-based task/memory isolation (FreeRTOS-MPU, Zephyr user mode) appears absent from the index; naming is diffuse so I did not add it — orchestrator may want a dedicated check. Index entries that look wrong/duplicated to me: (a) 'adapter' lists 'Decorator' as an aka — Decorator is a separate GoF pattern (which also appears nowhere else as its own entry except inside adapter's aka; the standalone 'decorator' element seems MISSING from the index entirely — worth an orchestrator check); (b) 'factory-method' lists 'Prototype, clone' in aka — Prototype is a distinct GoF pattern and also has no standalone entry; (c) setjmp-longjmp-exception-handling (457) and setjmp-longjmp-structured-error-handling (458) look like the same mechanism twice — merge candidate; (d) cache-eviction-policy (43) and lru-cache (276) substantially overlap (both enumerate LRU/LFU/CLOCK/2Q/ARC).
